Anthropic clarified that Claude did not access the state's voter registration system or change or pull any voting records. Axios first reported the action; Reuters is sourcing it.
items.title: Anthropic Says Claude Accessed Georgia Vote Data Behind Paywall

items.summary: A Haryana consumer commission directed Samsung India Electronics to refund Rs 88,000 for a Z Flip6 that developed display and heating problems during its warranty period. Complainant Vicky Kapoor bought the phone on December 18, 2024, from Guru Simran Mobile in Rohtak; it reportedly began overheating and dropping network calls within days, then failed to turn on by July 28, 2025. Samsung argued dents and scratches caused physical damage making repairs ineligible for warranty. The bench found no reliable evidence of such damage or a valid reason for the phone's status change from full to out of warranty, ruling in favour of deficiency in service. It ordered the refund after deducting 20 percent depreciation, plus 9 percent annual interest from August 22, 2025, Rs 5,000 compensation and Rs 5,000 litigation costs within 30 days.
items.title: Haryana Commission Orders Samsung Refund Over Z Flip6 Screen Failure

items.summary: Billionaire investor Peter Thiel renewed his criticism of Apple, arguing the company produced no meaningful innovation after Steve Jobs died in 2011. Speaking to author Walter Isaacson on The Builder's podcast per a Benzinga report, Thiel said "in my telling, it did nothing new after Jobs," citing the iPhone as such an invention that little remained to revolutionize.
items.title: Peter Thiel Repeats Apple Has Stopped Innovating Since Jobs

items.summary: Infosys shares fell 4 per cent on Monday after the IT services major cut its FY27 revenue growth guidance to 1-2 per cent in constant currency terms, from an earlier 1.5-3 per cent. The reduction came amid sluggish client spending and subdued volume growth, despite strong deal wins during the September quarter. Infosys reported revenue of ₹49,244 crore for the quarter, up 1.5 per cent year-on-year, with net profit rising 6.2 per cent to ₹7,823 crore. The cut marks a second consecutive quarter of downward revisions. Goldman Sachs flagged that the updated midpoint implies modestly negative organic growth, while Citi and UBS noted mixed signals on demand and valuation.
items.title: Infosys Cuts FY27 Revenue Growth Guidance as Shares Fall

items.summary: Infosys trimmed its revenue growth guidance for fiscal year 2027 (FY27) to a constant-currency range of 1-2%, down from the earlier 1.5-3% forecast, citing a challenging demand environment. The company reported that revenue from operations rose 11% year-on-year to Rs 49,244 crore in the period reviewed. It revised its FY27-28 forward guidance to 1.1%-2.0%, also below prior estimates of 1.2%-2.8%. The company attributed the cuts to pricing pressure from intensifying competition and softer volume growth in Q2FY27. Brokerages such as Nomura, Morgan Stanley, Citi and Choice Institutional Equities maintained their ratings while revising target prices; analysts noted strong bookings could partly offset headwinds but warned that a recovery depends on converting wins into revenue (summary,71 words)
items.title: Infosys Cuts FY27 Revenue Growth Guidance Amid Weak Outlook

items.summary: Shares of India's Infosys fell 2.7 per cent on Monday after the company sharply cut its fiscal 2027 revenue growth forecast to 1 per cent-2 per cent from 1.5 per cent-3 per cent, below most analysts' expectations. The move underscored AI-driven pricing pressure, tougher competition and sluggish demand in key markets. Analysts cited weaker volumes, smaller price increases and offshore delivery shifts as factors.
items.title: Infosys shares fall after revenue growth forecast cut

items.summary: Central banks worldwide have turned hawkish as inflationary pressures mount, with the Reserve Bank of India in October shifting its stance to calibrated tightening and raising its benchmark repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.5%—its first such move in nearly four years. Experts warn bond funds face a tricky phase amid rising yields, rupee pressure and imported inflation from elevated energy prices linked to the Iran-US war and Russian sanctions. Unlike the 2022 cycle, which began at record-low rates of 4%, this one starts higher at 5.25%. Most analysts expect a shallow hike path, with consensus projecting another 50-75 basis points. Advisers recommend shorter-duration bonds for capital preservation over chasing yields.
items.title: RBI Rate Hikes Prompt Cautious Debt Portfolios

items.summary: Singapore will raise its retirement age to 65 on Jan 1, 2029, and the re-employment age to 70, taking effect one year ahead of schedule. The Tripartite Workgroup on Senior Employment said the changes give senior workers assurance they can keep working if they wish. Recommendations were accepted by the Government after consultations with over 1,000 stakeholders. Among full-time resident employees aged 50 to 64, MOM data for 2024 showed 85.5% offered flexi-time work and 78.7% offered flexi-place arrangements, while just 74.5% were provided with flexi-load options. The workgroup proposed a new flexi-load programme replacing the Part-Time Re-employment Grant, which had supported about 68,500 seniors and 7,800 employers.
items.title: Singapore raises retirement age and expands flexi work for seniors

items.summary: Singapore's manufacturing output rose 3.4% year on year in September, according to data released by the Economic Development Board (EDB) on Oct 26, easing from August's 15.4%. The figure fell well short of a 7.1% economist forecast compiled for Bloomberg. Growth was driven mainly by AI-related demand supporting electronics and precision engineering, while pharmaceuticals contracted sharply.
items.title: Singapore factory output growth slows in September amid AI demand

items.summary: Louphou Coulibaly and Charles Engel examine optimal non-cooperative monetary policy in a two-country New Keynesian model with complete financial markets. They find that currency misalignments matter even for self-oriented policymakers, that full commitment accounts for asset values, and surprisingly that the strategic targeting rule matches cooperative policy because state-contingent claim prices offset terms-of-trade gains.
items.title: Coulibaly and Engel Study Strategic Monetary Policy in Open Economies

items.summary: Jin Huang and colleagues introduce HouseholdBench, an evaluation uniting six U.S. household surveys with 32 prediction tasks covering consumption, income, labor, expectations, and housing. Thirteen proprietary and open-weight models are tested against baseline methods; most beat the no-change benchmark, though gradient-boosted trees still lead overall.
items.title: HouseholdBench Evaluates LLMs on Household Economic Behavior

items.summary: Defence minister Rajnath Singh criticised Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge over a 'baap' remark about Prime Minister Narendra Modi, calling it an insult to India and an attack on the dignity of politics. Speaking Monday in New Delhi, he said Modi's resolve could not be weakened by such remarks. He accused Congress of defending and validating Kharge's words instead of expressing regret.
items.title: Rajnath Singh Calls Kharge Remark Insult to India

items.summary: NEW DELHI: Thick smoke was seen billowing from the Union secretariat's North Block on Monday, prompting authorities to rush six fire tenders to the spot, an official said. Delhi Fire Services received a call at 11.10 am reporting smoke emanating from the building, following which six fire tenders were dispatched, the official said. A police officer said some repair work was underway and might have led to a minor fire; no casualty has been reported so far.
items.title: Smoke Seen From North Block; Six Fire Tenders Rushed To Site

items.summary: The Yeyahu Wetland Nature Reserve in Beijing's Yanqing District has joined the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN) Green List, marking its first such accreditation in the region. Local authorities say over 13 square kilometers of degraded wetland have been restored through coordinated measures since the reserve was established in 1997. The site hosts more than 100,000 migratory birds annually and now serves as a platform for sharing biodiversity conservation stories across IUCN's network covering more than 60 countries.
items.title: Yeyahu Wetland Earns IUCN Green List Accreditation

items.summary: The 2026 Global Governance Forum in Xiongan, China, concluded on Sunday with the release of a document titled 'Global Governance: Xiongan Vision,' calling for stronger multilateral cooperation. Participants from 97 countries attended between October 23 and 25 under the theme 'Rebuilding Confidence and Cooperation.' The vision urged reforming global institutions, expanding Global South representation in decision-making, advancing sustainable development goals through 2030, and strengthening international collaboration on climate change, artificial intelligence, cyberspace, and outer space.
items.title: Xiongan Forum Calls for Stronger Multilateral Cooperation and Global Governance Reform

items.summary: Yu Xueyu, CEO of Schroders Hong Kong, told CGTN in an interview that the opening-up of China's capital market is a very positive long-term development. He said it deepens two-way connectivity between China and international capital markets.
items.title: Schroders CEO Praises China's Capital Market Opening as Positive Long-Term Development

items.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi praised Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath for improving law and order in Uttar Pradesh, saying a female worker at Arvind Textiles in Varanasi credited enhanced security for enabling women to work. The remark came during an interaction with employees before the state elections, where law and order is expected to be a major issue.
items.title: Modi Praises Yogi Adityanath Ahead of Uttar Pradesh Polls

items.summary: A weekly guide lists exhibitions, films, a TV series and music releases across Europe opening around 30 October 2026. It features an Agatha Christie exhibition at the British Library running until 20 June 2027, plus new film Wicker starring Olivia Colman and Peter Dinklage.
items.title: Sexy wicker and an Agatha Christie exhibition: The best things to do, hear, see or watch in Europe this week

items.summary: A political controversy erupted after Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge made remarks during an address in Patna concerning Prime Minister Narendra Modi. The Bharatiya Janata Party launched protests across Bengaluru, Delhi and Lucknow, with Home Minister Amit Shah accusing the Congress chief of crossing norms of decency by commenting against the PM and his late father. BJP leaders demanded a public apology from Kharge.
items.title: BJP Stages Protests After Kharge's Remarks on Modi

items.summary: Thousands filled São Paulo's Paulista Avenue with fireworks and chants as Brazilians celebrated President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva's win in Sunday's presidential runoff. The left-wing president took 51.8% of valid votes against Senator Flávio Bolsonaro's 48.2%, a margin of roughly 4.4 million votes, per the Superior Electoral Court. His victory overturned an earlier first-round deficit; Bolsonaro has refused to accept it and seeks annulment.
items.title: Brazilians Celebrate Lula's Fourth-Term Election Win

items.summary: Australian MPs paid tribute to Independent Member for Indi Helen Haines, who was attacked by a man driving at her outside her Wangaratta office last Monday, resulting in both legs being amputated. On Monday an orange cardboard bird sat in the parliament as colleagues delivered messages of support and reflected on her grassroots roots, advocacy for regional mental health services, and role establishing the National Anti-Corruption Commission (NACC). Prime Minister Anthony Albanese spoke of finding himself looking toward where she would normally sit, while Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke said words could reach someone 'on the edge'. Several politicians signed a Civility Pledge inspired by British MP Jo Cox. Independent MP Monique Ryan highlighted how one man hurt Haines but others ran to help.
items.title: Parliament honours MP Helen Haines after attack with civility pledge and cockatoo tribute

items.summary: The Hyderabad Metropolitan Water Supply and Sewerage Board has asked its offices to switch off air conditioners after 5 PM as part of a drive to cut water and electricity use. Managing Director K. Ashok Reddy issued the directions, saying conservation must begin within the organisation before officials ask citizens to save water. Every office must reduce consumption by at least 20% compared with its previous usage. Expected El Niño conditions are behind the emphasis on saving water. Under the rules, all ACs must be set at 25°C, and their use stops after 5 PM, except for essential maintenance approved by senior officials. Offices must also collect and reuse discharged water, repair leaks promptly, switch off lights and fans when unnecessary, review consumption regularly, and recognise offices that meet the target with appreciation certificates each month.
items.title: Hyderabad Water Board Asks Staff To Switch Off ACs After 5 PM

items.summary: A man's body was recovered from Smothering Creek on Boompa Road after an unusual weather system brought multiple storms and a days-long deluge to parts of Australia. Emergency services called him unresponsive shortly after 11am Monday; he was declared dead, with police preparing a coroner report. Six campers were rescued without injury at Leyburn campground. Torrential rain between Thursday and Monday flooded rivers across Queensland's south and east, with Blackdown Tableland recording 439.4mm to early Monday. Meteorologist Angus Hines described the atmospheric system as unusual.
items.title: Dead man found in Queensland flood waters amid storms

items.summary: A closed-door session of senior Chinese officials is underway in Beijing, where around 300 members of the Central Committee and state are gathered. State media said it would pave the way for a 'tightening of discipline' within the ruling Communist Party. The four-day gathering gives Xi Jinping an opportunity to consolidate his grip on power following recent purges.
items.title: China's Fifth Plenum May Tighten Party Discipline Under Xi

items.summary: Australia vice-captain Ashleigh Gardner says cricket has offered a welcome escape during a difficult period after her marriage broke down, thanking teammates for their support. Her former partner Monica Wright criticised the cricketer over her relationship with teammate Georgia Voll earlier this year. Cricket Australia was aware of the relationship before Wright's comments and backed Gardner to remain vice-captain. Speaking at the Sydney Sixers' season launch in Sydney on Monday, she said "Challenging, but cricket has been a fantastic escape," adding that winning the World Cup helped her maintain perspective.
items.title: Ashleigh Gardner credits cricket as refuge amid personal crisis

items.summary: A tourism company in Nanjo, Okinawa Prefecture has shelved plans for an exclusive early-morning tour of Sefa Utaki, a UNESCO World Heritage sanctuary. Operator DMO Nanjo decided at its Oct. 5 board meeting to scrap the plan for the current fiscal year amid opposition from local stakeholders. The firm said it would reconsider after building consensus among concerned parties.
items.title: Tourism Firm Shelves Okinawa Sanctuary Dawn Tour Over Local Pushback

items.summary: Senior officials from Türkiye, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan are set to visit Tehran for security talks with Iranian counterparts. Ali Bagheri of Iran's Supreme National Security Council told Iranian television that the meeting would promote a regional security framework in West Asia. The visiting delegation includes Saudi Defense Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman, Pakistani Chief of Army Staff Asim Munir, Turkish intelligence chief Ibrahim Kalin and others. Bagheri said officials would meet Mohsen Rezaei and President Masoud Pezeshkian to discuss regional security issues.
items.title: Turkish, Saudi and Pakistani Officials Set for Security Talks in Iran

items.summary: Challenger’s board rejected a $4.4 billion takeover offer from Daiichi Life Group, saying it would engage with the Japanese insurer’s Australian unit to seek an acceptable proposal. An indicative bid of 11.80 Australian dollars per share for the remaining 79.5% valued Challenger at about AU$7.9 billion ($5.5 billion). Shares were little changed Monday.
items.title: Challenger Rejects Daiichi Life Takeover Bid

items.summary: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi congratulated Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva on his re-election in Brazil, calling it remarkable and expressing hope to work closely with him. The victory positions Lula for a fourth non-consecutive term as India seeks partners for multilateral reform. Earlier, when the US imposed 50% tariffs on both countries in 2025, Modi and Lula pledged deeper cooperation across trade, energy, defence and technology. They agreed to raise bilateral trade to $30 billion by 2030, building on a 25% increase in 2025. The two sides have collaborated at BRICS and the G20, with Brazil holding among the world's largest rare earth reserves. Foreign Editor Rezaul Hasan Laskar of the Hindustan Times wrote the piece.
items.title: Modi and Lula pledge closer ties after Brazil's election

items.summary: Bloomberg reported that Saudi Arabia agreed with Singapore to store crude oil in underground caverns at the Jurong Rock Caverns, deliveries beginning next year's second half. The arrangement follows Houthi attacks on Saudi infrastructure and a Persian Gulf–Red Sea war disrupting exports, prompting Aramco ship-to-ship transfers near Oman. Officials said it boosts supply-chain resilience for both nations.
items.title: Saudi Arabia Signs Crude Storage Deal With Singapore

items.summary: Four young men were charred to death and a fifth critically injured after their vehicle struck a culvert divider, fell off it and caught fire around 11.30pm Sunday near Badnawar in Dhar district, police said Monday. Three bodies have been identified for autopsy; the survivor was referred to Indore. A case has been registered and an investigation is underway.
items.title: Four friends killed in fiery car crash on Madhya Pradesh highway

items.summary: Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva won his presidential runoff on Sunday with 51.7% of the vote to Senator Flávio Bolsonaro’s 48.2%, a margin of four million votes. He became the first president in Brazil’s history to win after losing the opening round, securing a fourth term and dealing a blow to the far right. The race ended amid chaos from an election extension ordered by a judge minutes before closing time at 7 p.m., which may fuel doubts about the vote. Flávio Bolsonaro called for annulment of the result. Lula credited social media mobilization over Instagram and WhatsApp, while his rival questioned voting reliability; Jair Bolsonaro had earlier been convicted in a coup attempt.
items.title: Lula Wins Historic Brazilian Runoff, Defeats Flávio Bolsonaro

items.summary: TCL SunPower, a unit of TCL Zhonghuan, introduced the SunPower Origin series for residential rooftops. The top module, SPR-BE54-HD505, delivers 505 W at 24. 7% efficiency using eighth-generation back-contact cells in a fully black design. Director Karin Alberto-Burkhardt told pv magazine that its format fits more modules on irregular or partially obstructed rooftops. The five versions range from 485 W to 505 W, with efficiencies between 23. 8% and 24. 7%. Modules measure 1,800 mm × 1,134 mm × 30 mm and weigh 26 kg. They carry a Class A+ shading-resistance certification from TÜV Rheinland and a 40-year warranty covering product, power output and service.
items.title: TCL SunPower Launches High-Efficiency Back-Contact Rooftop Panel

items.summary: Defence personnel at Sydney's 176-year-old Victoria Barracks have begun packing boxes ahead of a Christmas eviction, according to Defence sources quoted by the ABC. NSW Premier Chris Minns has called on the federal government to reverse its decision to sell the site among 67 earmarked properties expected to raise up to $3 billion. Defence Minister Richard Marles defended the move, citing office work and costs.
items.title: NSW Premier Urges Reversal of Victoria Barracks Sale as Eviction Looms

items.summary: Kenya's transport safety authority is calling for road crashes to be declared a 'national emergency' after 24 people died in a head-on collision on the Nairobi–Mombasa highway. At least 24 others were injured, with passengers returning from a funeral in western Kenya. Authorities say improper overtaking caused it; Reverend Spencier Mdave described how the truck tried to overtake and lost control. President Ruto ordered inspections of all public service vehicles and urged drivers to observe traffic rules. The crash came three weeks after 17 died on the same highway, amid reports that about 20,000 crashes claim more than 5,000 lives a year.
items.title: Kenya transport authority calls road crashes a national emergency after bus crash kills 24

items.summary: Jordanian security forces arrested three suspects over a Friday gun attack on Hamoud Church during a funeral in the southern Karak governorate, an official said Monday. The assault killed nine people and injured 25 others. Spokesman Mohammad al-Momani reported that the suspects opened fire on security forces during a raid before being captured wounded; no officers were hurt, and weapons were seized at the scene.
items.title: Jordan Arrests Suspects in Church Attack That Killed Nine

items.summary: Analysts say Brazil faces deep economic problems from high public spending, stubborn inflation and low saving. These produce a cost of capital that some analysts put at 9% or more in real terms—higher than Russia and four times peers like Chile, the Philippines and South Africa. A rigid constitution forces mandatory spending to 90% of the federal budget, while weak savings, at 14% of GDP, keep Brazilians from building reserves.
items.title: Brazil's economic troubles need true Milei-like ardour to fix

items.summary: Much of London's Oxford Street will be closed to motorised traffic from Monday as the long-awaited pedestrianisation begins. About half of the street, containing John Lewis and Selfridges, will be vehicle-free between 7am on 26 October until midnight every day. Private cars were already barred during daytime hours; this extends the ban around the clock to buses, black cabs and bikes.
items.title: London pedestrianises Oxford Street in first phase of scheme

items.summary: In Hebron, a gun attack on an Israeli checkpoint killed two soldiers and prompted Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to vow sweeping retribution ahead of Tuesday's elections. By Sunday morning the city was sealed off and the neighbourhood of Farsh al-Hawa had been flattened. The Hebron municipality said 370 families, nearly 2,000 people, had been displaced by an army sweep through Ein Deir Baha. In its statement, the Israeli military claimed the residents left voluntarily and that many belonged to the Jaba'a clan linked to Hamas; local residents disputed both claims, numbering the clan at about 150. Hebron's mayor Yousef al-Jabari called it collective punishment.
items.title: Nearly 2,000 Palestinians displaced in Hebron as Israeli forces seize homes

items.summary: Neoenergia and the European Investment Bank signed an R$857m (€153m) financing agreement to modernise and expand Neoenergia Elektro’s electricity distribution network in São Paulo and Mato Grosso do Sul. The loan, provided through EIB Global and guaranteed by Spain’s Cesce, will fund upgrades to lines, substations and grid automation, reduce technical losses, support new connections and renewable integration, and improve resilience during extreme weather. Eduardo Capelastegui said the financing reinforces Neoenergia’s commitment to preparing the grid for new energy demands.
items.title: Neoenergia and EIB Sign Grid Modernisation Financing Deal

items.summary: Starting November 1, new rules and price updates affect Indian households using Indane, HP Gas, and Bharatgas. Consumers must complete biometric Aadhaar authentication to keep subsidies uninterrupted; Jagran reported that those who fail may be blocked from subsidised refills until verification finishes. Users can authenticate via their OMC app or through distributors during delivery. Those opting out will buy only 5-kg or 10-kg cylinders at market rates, per a report cited by the article. Domestic LPG prices have stayed stable; a 14.2-kg cylinder retails at ₹942 in Delhi, unchanged since June 7, while commercial rates rose to ₹2,810 for a 19-kg cylinder in October.
items.title: New LPG Cylinder Rules Take Effect in November

items.summary: A court in Sultanpur, Uttar Pradesh acquitted Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Monday of a criminal defamation case over his 2018 remarks calling Union Home Minister Amit Shah a "murder accused." The Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate found the comments not defamatory. The case had been filed by BJP leader Vijay Mishra after remarks made during the Karnataka elections.
items.title: Court Acquits Rahul Gandhi in Defamation Case Over Remarks About Amit Shah

items.summary: Modular solar specialist 5B has executed a purchase order with 1414 Degrees to deliver 70 MW of prefabricated Maverick units for the initial stage of South Australia’s Aurora Energy Precinct project. The deployment covers 42 hectares within an approved 200-hectare footprint, alongside a battery energy storage system and proposed grid connections. Executive Chairman Kevin Moriarty called it a major milestone as power purchase agreements and financing progress.
items.title: Modular Solar Builder Wins Order for Australian Precinct

items.summary: A special MP/MLA court in Sultanur dismissed a defamation case against Congress leader Rahul Gandhi, who had been acquitted of remarks allegedly made against Union Home Minister Amit Shah during a May 2018 press conference. The complaint, filed by Vijay Mishra and pursued for nearly eight years under Section 500 of the Indian Penal Code, was dropped after hearings spanning from 2018 to October 26, 2026. Detailed grounds were not immediately available.
items.title: Sultanpur Court Acquits Rahul Gandhi in Defamation Case

items.summary: The Mumbai Litfest announced its 2026 winners for the Literature Live! Literary Awards on Sunday across five categories, aiming to recognise literary talent in fiction, nonfiction and business. Irwin Allan Sealy received the Lifetime Achievement Award while Gagan Gill was named Poet Laureate; Westland Books won Publisher of the Year. The awards cover established and new writers.
items.title: Mumbai Litfest Names 2026 Literature Live! Winners

items.summary: Eric Bauza, the Emmy award-winning voice artist behind Bugs Bunny, Daffy Duck and Porky Pig, has died at age 46. His family posted a statement on Instagram saying he had died suddenly. Variety reports the cause was hypertensive cardiovascular disease and that he died at home on Sunday. He voiced characters in Space Jam: A New Legacy and Coyote vs. Acme, won three Emmys between 2022 and 2025, and appeared in The Super Mario Bros. Movie. Channing Dungey of Warner Bros. Television Group said Bauza brought joy to millions around the world and followed in the footsteps of Mel Blanc.
items.title: Eric Bauza, Looney Tunes voice actor, dies aged 46

items.summary: Uganda's health ministry announced Sunday that Ugandans returning from DR Congo will undergo a mandatory 21-day quarantine at their own cost, following the country's worst-ever Ebola outbreak. The ministry said it has intensified screening at Entebbe International Airport and all land border crossings. Uganda was declared Ebola-free in August after 20 cases; the current Bundibugyo strain outbreak in DRC has caused more than 4,600 deaths since May.
items.title: Uganda Mandates 21-Day Quarantine for Travelers From DRC Amid Ebola Outbreak

items.summary: A Sultanpur court acquitted Congress leader Rahul Gandhi of a 2018 criminal defamation case filed by BJP leader Vijay Mishra over remarks about Amit Shah made at a Bengaluru rally ahead of the 2018 Karnataka Assembly elections. The court ruled his comments did not amount to defamation, and he had secured bail in 2023.
items.title: Rahul Gandhi Acquitted in Defamation Case Over Remarks on Amit Shah

items.summary: Crude oil prices dipped this week but stayed high amid ongoing Middle East tensions, with Brent at $114.42 per barrel and West Texas Intermediate above $100. A record number of tanker attacks occurred in the Strait of Hormuz this month, according to data from UK Maritime Trade Operations and the International Maritime Organization as reported by Reuters. The actual toll is likely higher since not all incidents are reported.
items.title: Houthi and Iranian Attacks Keep Crude Above $100 Despite Weekly Dip

items.summary: Ahead of Israel’s national elections on Tuesday, October 27, opinion polls place Gadi Eisenkot’s Yashar Party ahead of Benjamin Netanyahu’s Likud. The average across several polls puts the gap at about 4.5 seats, though neither party is expected to reach the 61-seat majority needed in the Knesset’s 120 lawmakers. A Channel 13 poll quoted by the Jerusalem Post projects a “change bloc” of anti-Netanyahu parties with 54 seats versus 50 for Likud loyalists; among individual parties, Yashar leads narrowly on 23 seats to Likud’s 21. Eisenkot has declared readiness to form a minority government backed from outside, but Netanyahu retains coalition experience and the support of religious and right-wing allies. As one voter put it: “The current prime minister is the strongest and most experienced leader we have.” Forming any government remains uncertain unless voters change their minds.
items.title: Polls edge toward opposition but no majority looms

items.summary: Congress leader Kunwar Danish Ali sparked a political controversy with his remark 'naajayaz aulaadein' (illegitimate offspring) while defending party president Mallikarjun Kharge's comments against Prime Minister Narendra Modi during an event in Patna. The statement, delivered amid escalating Congress–BJP tensions, warned that alleged electoral malpractitioners would face consequences.
items.title: Congress Leader Danish Ali Targets Modi With Illegitimate Offspring Remark

items.summary: Tripartite partners in Singapore announced on Monday (Oct 26) measures to encourage older workers to keep working, including raising the statutory retirement and re-employment ages from 64 and 69 currently to 65 and 70 from 2029. The change means employers cannot dismiss employees for age before they turn 65 and must offer re-employment until they are 70. Other measures extend wage support, raise assistance for lower-wage seniors and enhance Earned Income Relief of up to S$8,000 for workers aged 55 and above. A new Flexi-Load Programme will replace the Part-time Re-employment Grant from 2027, covering workers aged 50 and above. Minister of State for Manpower Dinesh Vasu Dash said seniors who wish to work longer would have the opportunity to do so.
items.title: Singapore raises retirement ages and expands support for older workers

items.summary: Bharat Coking Coal reported a profit after tax of Rs 123.7 crore in the quarter ended September 30, 2026, reversing an Rs 53 crore loss a year earlier. Revenue from operations rose 39% YoY to Rs 4,412.58 crore. Shares rallied about 5%, though they remain down around 11% over three months and trade below all seven simple moving averages.
items.title: Bharat Coking Coal Shares Rise on Q2 Profit Turnaround

items.summary: Frances Lee argues that losing candidates conceding is central to democratic legitimacy, noting the overwhelming majority of losers acknowledged defeat in 2020 and 2022 congressional races examined by Bright Line Watch. She cites improved election administration since 2020, with shorter voting waits reported across racial groups by 2024.
items.title: Frances Lee on American elections

items.summary: Shriram Finance shares fell about 6% in morning trade, dropping to Rs 811 on the NSE. The company reported a 59% year-on-year rise in standalone net profit to Rs 3,677 crore for the quarter ended September 2026, supported by higher net interest income and lower finance costs. Jefferies cut its target price to Rs 1,145 from Rs 1,210 while keeping a Buy call; Citi reduced its target to Rs 1,100 from Rs 1,200 but maintained Buy; Motilal Oswal slashed the target to Rs 1,155 and also kept Buy. The writer is not an SEBI-registered analyst or investment adviser.
items.title: Shriram Finance Shares Fall as Brokers Cut Targets Despite Buy Calls

items.summary: An unattributed report states Western luxury brands lost roughly $280 billion in value this year as Chinese consumers spent more on domestic products but less overall. A Council on Foreign Relations expert argues that rising similarity between China and the West's export baskets could intensify existing trade tensions.
items.title: Western luxury brands lose value amid China's domestic shift

items.summary: A new Apollo analysis found that corporate America's large AI investments have produced zero financial payoff outside the Magnificent 7, intensifying investor fears ahead of major Big Tech earnings. Investors show little patience for higher capital spending without proof of returns amid elevated interest and energy costs.
items.title: Apollo Analysis Finds No AI Payoff Outside Magnificent 7

items.summary: A video circulating on social media claimed to show Maharashtra FDA chief Tukaram Mundhe supporting protesters demanding Gyanesh Kumar's resignation. The Quint fact-checked the claim as false, using a Google Lens reverse image search that traced it to an original upload by The Times of India showing Mundhe at Sydenham College of Commerce and Economics in Mumbai during Management Conclave '26.
items.title: Fact-checker Debunks Viral Video Claiming Tukaram Mundhe at Anti-CEC Protest

items.summary: After nearly two weeks of protests, hunger strikes and campus lockdowns at Jamia Millia Islamia, the administration agreed to conduct student union elections and revoke disciplinary actions taken since 12 October. Students had demanded restoration of the Jamia Millia Islamia Students’ Union, which has not held elections since 2005 or 2006. The university formed a draft constitution committee and cited compliance with Lyngdoh Committee recommendations. Organisers said they would monitor follow-through.
items.title: Jamia Millia Islamia Agrees to Hold Student Union Elections
